captions.text: I don't remember her face. I stand in that field every night... and the fog keeps it.
But her hand — that, I remember. The way it hummed when she held mine. Like the song lived in her skin... and she was letting me borrow it.
That's the cruel part about remembering. You hold on as hard as you can... and then the memory does what it always does.
It lets go first. Not her. Just the remembering.
I've spent my whole life walking back to that field. Not to find her —
— to remember what it felt like... to be held.
